runs.text: HANDWRITING OF ORDINANCES:
1. What does God blot out?
Acts 3:19
Repent ye therefore, and be converted,
that your sins may be blotted out.
Psalm 51:1
Have mercy upon me, O God,
blot out my transgressions.
Psalm 51:9
Hide thy face from my sins, and
blot out all mine iniquities
Note:
When our sins are forgiven, God blots them out of existence.

The death of God’s Son paid the penalty for our sins and those who believe in Him are forgiven. When God forgives, He hides His face from our sins and they no longer exist. (See Psalm 51:9) To blot out means to obliterate, erase, wipe out. (See Strong’s)
Some falsely teach that, instead of God blotting out our transgressions, that He blots out the existence of the Ten Commandments by nailing them to the cross.
2. What was blotted out and nailed to the cross?
Colossians 2:14
Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us
, which was contrary to us, and
took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.
Note:
Put simply, it was the record of our violations of God’s Commandments that were nailed to the cross. God’s Law remains intact.

Christ died on the cross to pay the penalty for man’s sins. The handwriting that was against us is the record of our sins. It was God’s Son that was nailed to the cross. Christ went to the cross to pay man’s penalty.
3. What are the dead judged out of?
Revelation 20:12
And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and
the books were opened
: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and
the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.
Note:

The handwriting that is against us is the record that the unbelievers will be judged out of, according to their works. The believers’ names will be written in the book of life. The record of believers’ sins will be blotted out during the latter rain when the refreshing comes. (See Acts 3:19)
ANNUAL SABBATHS:
4. But wasn’t the Sabbath nailed to the cross?
Colossians 2:16
Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days
Which are a shadow of things to come.
Note:
This text is speaking about the annual Sabbaths, also known as feast days. When we read verse 17 it becomes clear that this is speaking about the shadow of things to come.
Which are a shadow of things to come
” (Colossians 2:
The feast days were the shadow pointing to the coming Messiah
This text is not talking about the weekly Sabbath.
5. Colossians 2:16
17 is quoting Ezekiel 45:17.
Ezekiel 45:17
to give burnt offerings, and
meat offerings, and drink offerings,
in the feasts
and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths.
Note:

Colossians 2:16-17 is a quote from Ezekiel 45:17. Reading the text from Ezekiel 45:17 helps us understand that Paul was referring to the ceremonial Sabbaths. It even mentions the word ‘feast’ in this text.
These verses are referring to the ceremonial feast Sabbaths that the Jews kept, looking forward to Christ. The Ten Commandments were not nailed to the cross.
FAITH ESTABLISHES THE LAW:
6. Does faith do away with the law?
Romans 3:31
Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.
Note:
Many teach that the Ten Commandments were done away with. God’s law can never be done away with because it is the foundation of His government.
God’s law is His law of love. The plan of salvation re-establishes the law of God’s love in the hearts of converted men. (See Gal 5:14, Romans 8:4)
7. How much shall pass from the law?
Matthew 5:18
For verily I say unto you,
Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
Note:

When we are born again, God changes our heart. As we begin to behold His love, our hearts will begin to beat in harmony with the law, and we will become lights to the world. (See Matt 5:14) God desires this light to be seen of men. We are to let this light shine so others can see the law of love in our hearts and glorify our Father in heaven. (See Matt 5:15-17)
RIGHTEOUSNESS - IS THE LAW OF LOVE:
8. What is righteousness?
Psalm 119:172
My tongue shall speak of thy word:
for all thy commandments are righteousness.
Note:
The commandments are righteousness. Not just in the abstract, but they ARE the righteousness of God. Question #9 offers proof that the Com-mandments are the righteousness of God.
9. What is in those who know righteousness?
Isaiah 51:6
But my salvation shall be for ever, and
my righteousness shall not be abolished.
Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law
Note:
What do we learn from this? They who know the righteousness of God are those in whose heart is His law, and therefore that the law of God in the heart is the righteousness of God.
10. What does love fulfill?
Romans 13:10
Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law
Note:

God is love. Man in his natural state loves only himself. Our characters can reflect God’s love only as we behold Him, and walk in the Spirit. Then the love of God shines forth from Christ, and on to others through us. (See also Galatians 5:14)
TRANSGRESSION OF GOD’S LAW IS SIN:
11. What is the definition of sin?
1 John 3:4
Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law
Note:

Sin is transgression of the law, and is also unrighteousness. (See 1 John 5:17) Therefore sin and unrighteousness are identical. Since sin is the transgression of the law; therefore righteousness must be obedience to the law.
12. Which law defines sin?
Romans 7:7
What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay,
I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.
Note:
Thou shalt not covet is one of the Ten Commandments. Therefore the Ten Commandments are the measure of the righteousness of God. There is, indeed, no other righteousness.
THE LAW JUDGES EVEN OUR THOUGHTS:
13. What is the whole duty of man?
Ecclesiastes 12:13
Fear God, and keep his com-mandments: for this is the whole duty of man
Note:
Keeping the Ten Commandments is the whole duty of man.
Let no one think that his duty is confined to just the letter of the Ten Commandments. The Com-mandments are “exceedingly broad” (Psalm 119:96).
14. How many works are brought into judgment?
Ecclesiastes 12:13
Fear God, and keep his com-mandments: for this is the whole duty of man. 14
For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil
Note:
The reach of the Ten Commandments contains the moral duty of every creature. In short, it is the measure of the righteousness of God. It judges the thought and intent of every act of our entire life.
15. Does the law judge even our thoughts?
Matthew 5:28
That
whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.
Note:
Even our thoughts will be judged by the law.
16. If you break only one part of the law, what else have you broken?
James 2:10
For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.
Note:

For one to be judged “a doer of the law.’ you would have had to keep the law every moment of your life. You could not be a doer of the law if you did it only in part. There is no hope for anyone trying to become righteous by the letter of the law unless he has kept the law perfectly his entire life. If we have failed in any way, our case becomes hopeless.
OUR ONLY HOPE IS IN CHRIST:
17. How many have sinned?
Romans 3:23
For all have sinned
, and come short of the glory of God.
Note:
Some have thought that if they could just
slow down their sinning
or, if it were even possible,
stop sinning altogether
, that they would be okay and could be saved from God’s wrath. However, this doesn’t solve the problem of past sins and guilt.
18. How does the sinner obtain righteousness?
Romans 4:5
But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly
his faith is
counted for righteousness.
Note:

Justification is a free gift from God. (See Rom 3:24) We receive justification by faith, apart from keeping the law. By faith, Christ’s righteousness is credited to our account. This free gift of righteousness does not change or alter the law, it establishes the law.
19. How are we saved from the law’s death penalty?
John 3:16
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that
whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
Note:

The law demands the death of the transgressor. God could not change or alter His law to save us. What He did instead, was He paid this penalty for us through the death of His son. The death of the Son of God applies to the record of all who believe in him.
The purpose of this study is to discover why God’s law of love is so important that it requires a death penalty.
TEN COMMANDMENTS:
20. What did God ask Moses to build?
Exodus 25:10
And they shall
make an ark of shittim wood:
… And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold.
21. What was placed on top of the ark?
Exodus 25:17
And thou shalt make a mercy seat of pure gold:
two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof. 18
And thou shalt make two cherubims of gold, of beaten work shalt thou make them, in the two ends of the mercy seat.

19 And make one cherub on the one end, and the other cherub on the other end: even of the mercy seat shall ye make the cherubims on the two ends thereof. 20 And the cherubims shall stretch forth their wings on high, covering the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces shall look one to another; toward the mercy seat.
Note:
Cherubim are angels. God told Moses to build a mercy seat. This seat was to be overlaid with Gold and was to have two golden angels looking over it.
22. What was placed inside of the ark?
Exodus 25:21
And thou shalt put the mercy seat above upon the ark; and in the ark thou shalt put the testimony that I shall give thee.
Note:
The testimony is the Ten Commandments that were placed under the mercy seat.
23. In Which part of the earthly tabernacle was the ark containing the testimony then placed?
Hebrews 9:3
And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;
4 Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded,
and the tables of the covenant;
And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat.
Note:

The ark was placed in the Most Holy place of the earthly tabernacle. (Hebrews 9:3-5) No man could enter this area except the high priest, and he only entered once a year. (See Hebrews 9:7) Even then he could not see the ark because there was a cloud of smoke arising from the incense censer which he held in his hand, entirely concealing it. (See Lev. 16:12, 13.) Without this precaution, the high priest would have died due to God’s presence.
24 Where did God meet with Israel?
Exodus 25:21
And
thou shalt put the mercy seat above upon the ark;
and in the ark thou shalt put the testimony that I shall give thee.
And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims
Note:
God met with Israel and conversed with them above the mercy seat. Below the mercy seat was the “testimony”, which is the Ten Commandment Law.
THE EARTHLY TABERNACLE WAS PATTERNED AFTER A BUILDING IN HEAVEN:
25. Where did Moses see the pattern for the earthly tabernacle?
Exodus 25:9
According to all that I shew thee, after the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all the instruments thereof, even so shall ye make it. 40
And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount.
Note:
Since it was to be God’s house, God himself furnished a pattern for it. The earthly tabernacle was an exact copy of the one located in heaven.
26. Where is the true sanctuary located?
Hebrews 9:23
It was therefore necessary that
the patterns of things in the heavens
should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these. 24 For
Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us.
Note:

This tells us plainly that the tabernacle and its furniture was copied after things in the Heavens. Christ now appears in the presence of God for us. Jesus appears before God as our high priest to atone for His people.
FOUNDATION OF GOD’S THRONE:
27. What does John see in the heavenly temple?
Revelation 11:19
Then the temple of God was opened in heaven, and the ark of His covenant was seen in His temple
Note:

The earthly tabernacle built by Moses as a dwelling-place for God was only a temporary representation of God’s real, permanent dwelling-place in his temple in Heaven. God does have a tangible dwelling place in Heaven.
When John sees the temple in Heaven, the ark containing the law is there. God’s actual dwelling-place in heaven is between the cherubim.
For proof of this, read the following texts:—
Psalm 80:1
“Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, You who lead Joseph like a flock;
You who dwell between the cherubim
, shine forth!”
Psalm 99:1. “
The LORD reigns; let the people tremble!
He dwells between the cherubim
; Let the earth be moved!”
(See also Ezekiel 1:10; Isaiah 6:1-3)
Note:

Everything in the earthly sanctuary was a representation of some corresponding thing in the heavenly sanctuary. It was made as nearly exact as human hands could approach to a likeness of things made by God. The throne made by God in Heaven includes the ark of His covenant. This throne is a living throne. The Ten Commandments in living form are not only written on literal tables of stone. The Ten commandments in living form are the love that exists in the heart of God.
28. What are the foundations of God’s throne?
Psalm 89:14
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne.
(NIV)
Note:
The righteousness that is the foundation of His throne is the heart of God. God is love. This love in its written form is the Ten Commandment law.

God’s law of love is so holy and so important, that to destroy it would in fact allow a different element to govern. It would allow for a spirit other than that of love to be the foundation of God’s throne.
29. How long will God’s throne and righteous law of love endure?
Psalm 119:160
Every one of
thy righteous judgments endureth for ever
Note:
Not one jot or one tittle can pass from the law. It will endure just as long as God’s throne endures.
Matt 5:18
Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law.
30. Why did God condemn sin in our flesh?
Romans 8:3
For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh,
God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin,
condemned sin in the flesh:
That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
Note:
The righteousness of the law of love can be restored in us when we walk in the Spirit.

Breaking God’s law of love has a death penalty attached to it. The sinful heart of man is capable of inflicting some of the most heinous acts of horror. Do we really want these horrors to continue to infect the new earth? It is for this reason that God in His wisdom has secured His perfect law of love with a death penalty. Sin will never be allowed to resurface.

God did not change the death penalty to save man. He demonstrated His wisdom in safeguarding love’s rule for evermore. If God could have done away with His law of love, or if it could have been changed, then His Son would not have had to die to pay its penalty. Jesus did die. He died for the sins of the entire world.

God’s Ten Commandment law was not nailed to the cross. Righteousness and judgment endure forever. They are the foundation of God’s throne in heaven. God’s throne is a living throne and the Ten Commandments reflect the righteousness that lives in God’s heart of love.
It was the record of the sins of believers that were nailed to the cross. The Ten Commandments are the righteousness, judgement, and love that beats in the heart of God!
Romans 13:10
Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore
love is the fulfilling of the law
(See context)
31. Which law does love fulfill?
(Context )
Romans 13:9
Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet.
Note:
The Ten Commandments were not nailed to the cross. Love fulfills the Ten Commandments law!
